summary: The appeals challenged the Allahabad High Court's dismissal of the appellants' appeals and confirmation of their conviction under Sections 302/149, 307/149, and 148 IPC. The prosecution relied on testimonies of Omveer (PW-1) and Inder (PW-2), both relatives of the deceased, and recoveries under Section 27 of the Evidence Act. The trial and High Court relied on these to convict. The appellants argued false implication, unreliability of witnesses, contradictions in medical and injury timing, non-examination of key witnesses (Kripa, Omwati, Vijay Singh), and suppression of station diary entries. The prosecution defended the credibility of ocular witnesses and corroborative recoveries. The Supreme Court noted Omveer did not witness the incident, as held even by the trial court. Inder, as an injured witness, had greater evidentiary value under Jarnail Singh and Abdul Sayeed. However, inconsistencies in testimony and lack of corroboration raised doubts. The Court re-examined evidence due to possible error in concurrent findings.
legal_provisions_cited: Jarnail Singh and Others v. State of Punjab (2009) 9 SCC 719
Abdul Sayeed v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2010) 10 SCC 259
Smt. Dalbir Kaur and Others v. State of Punjab (1976) 4 SCC 158
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed, the judgments of the High Court and trial court were quashed, and the appellants were acquitted due to insufficient reliable evidence and material contradictions in the prosecution case, despite the evidentiary weight of injured witness testimony.
